forbidden.name: core-is-self-contained
forbidden.comment: core is the innermost layer: it holds what every other layer may depend on, so it may depend on none of them. Anything core needs from downstream is a sign the concept belongs downstream too.

forbidden.name: domain-knows-only-core
forbidden.comment: The domain models the problem. It may lean on core, never on a use case, an adapter or a screen — otherwise the rules become unusable outside the app that happens to host them.

forbidden.name: usecases-own-their-ports
forbidden.comment: A use case declares the port it needs and lets infrastructure implement it. Importing infrastructure directly inverts that and nails the use case to one adapter.

forbidden.name: infrastructure-serves-and-does-not-render
forbidden.comment: Infrastructure implements the ports the inner layers declare. Reaching into the app layer would make an adapter depend on the screen that happens to use it.

forbidden.name: no-rendering-below-app
forbidden.comment: React, React Native and Expo Router render. A rule, a use case or an adapter that imports one can no longer be exercised without a renderer, which is what keeps the inner layers testable in plain Bun.

forbidden.name: inner-layers-are-platform-free
forbidden.comment: core, domain and usecases state the problem and its rules; they must hold on any platform. Wrapping a platform SDK is infrastructure's job, which is why it is allowed there and nowhere above it.

forbidden.name: no-circular
forbidden.comment: A cycle makes the two modules one module that happens to be stored in two files: neither can be read, tested or replaced on its own.

forbidden.name: not-to-dev-dep
forbidden.comment: Application code must not reach a devDependency: it is absent from a production install, so the failure appears at runtime in the bundle, not here.

forbidden.name: no-orphans
forbidden.comment: A module nothing imports is either dead or wired by a path the graph cannot see. Both are worth knowing about.
